lessons.title: What Are Selectors?
lessons.content: Selectors target HTML elements to apply styles. Types include element (e.g., p), class (.my-class), and ID (#my-id).

lessons.title: Class vs ID Selectors
lessons.content: Classes (.class) can be reused on multiple elements; IDs (#id) are unique. Example: .blue {color: blue;} or #header {background: grey;}

lessons.title: Understanding the Box Model
lessons.content: Every HTML element is a box with content, padding (inner space), border, and margin (outer space).

lessons.title: What is Float?
lessons.content: The float property (e.g., float: left) moves elements to the left or right, allowing text and inline elements to wrap around them.

lessons.title: What are Pseudo-Elements?
lessons.content: Pseudo-elements like ::before and ::after style specific parts of an element or add content, e.g., p::before {content: '★';}

lessons.content: ::before adds content before an element, ::after adds after, ::first-line styles the first line of text, and ::first-letter styles the first letter.
